from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Define high-level context
        title = "Prerequisite: The Complex Playground"

            'The complex plane has real and imaginary axes.',

            'It is a playground where numbers can turn and spin.'

        H_COLOR_3 = "#FFD700" # Gold for spinning playground

        self.lecture[0].set_color(H_COLOR_1)
        
        # Origin is at D4
        origin = self.grid["D4"]
        
        # Real Axis (Horizontal) from D2 to D6
        real_axis = Line(start=self.grid["D2"], end=self.grid["D6"], color=WHITE)
        # Imaginary Axis (Vertical) from F4 to A4
        imag_axis = Line(start=self.grid["F4"], end=self.grid["A4"], color=WHITE)
        
        # Labels for axes - Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        re_label = Text("Re", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(re_label, "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        re_label.shift(RIGHT * 0.4)
        
        im_label = Text("Im", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(im_label, "A4", scale_factor=1.0)
        im_label.shift(UP * 0.4)

        self.play(
            Create(real_axis), 
            Create(imag_axis), 
            Write(re_label), 
            Write(im_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(H_COLOR_2)
        
        # Dot at (1, 0) corresponds to grid D5
        dot = Dot(point=self.grid["D5"], color=WHITE)
        one_label = Text("1", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(one_label, "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        one_label.shift(DOWN * 0.4 + RIGHT * 0.2)
        
        i_label = Text("i", color=H_COLOR_2, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC)
        self.place_at_grid(i_label, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        i_label.shift(LEFT * 0.4 + UP * 0.2)

            start_angle=0, 
            angle=PI/2, 
            arc_center=origin, 
            color=H_COLOR_2

        minus_i_label.shift(LEFT * 0.4 + DOWN * 0.2)

        arc_to_neg1 = Arc(
            radius=1.0, 
            start_angle=PI/2, 
            angle=PI/2, 
            arc_center=origin, 
            color=H_COLOR_3
        )
        arc_to_negi = Arc(
            radius=1.0, 
            start_angle=PI, 
            angle=PI/2, 
            arc_center=origin, 
            color=H_COLOR_3
        )
        
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(dot, arc_to_neg1),
            Create(arc_to_neg1),
            Write(minus_one_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(dot, arc_to_negi),
            Create(arc_to_negi),
            Write(minus_i_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        lecture_lines = [
            "Real powers of e represent continuous outward growth.",
            "But an imaginary power i changes the direction.",
            "Instead of growing larger, the value starts to turn.",
            "It is like a side-thruster creating a circular orbit.",
            "Constant speed, but always changing the movement angle."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Growth vs. Rotation: The Role of 'e'", lecture_lines)

        # Coordinate System for the right side
        # Centering axes around D3/D4 area
        plane_center = self.grid["D3"]
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-0.5, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_C},
            tips=False
        ).move_to(plane_center)
        
        real_label = Text("Real", font_size=16, color=GREY_C).next_to(axes.x_axis.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        imag_label = Text("Imaginary", font_size=16, color=GREY_C).next_to(axes.y_axis.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Dot representing e^x
        growth_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        growth_dot.move_to(axes.c2p(1, 0)) # starts at e^0 = 1
        
        # Label for growth (Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency)
        growth_label = Text("e^x", color=YELLOW, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(growth_label, "A3")
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(real_label), Write(imag_label), FadeIn(growth_dot), Write(growth_label))
        
        # Growth animation: e^x moves from 1 to 2.5
        growth_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        growth_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(axes.c2p(np.exp(growth_tracker.get_value()), 0)))
        
        self.play(growth_tracker.animate.set_value(0.9), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # Change label to e^ix (Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency)
        rotation_label = Text("e^ix", color=BLUE, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(rotation_label, "A3")
        
        # Reset dot to 1 for the transition to circular motion
        growth_dot.clear_updaters()
        self.play(
            FadeOut(growth_label),
            FadeIn(rotation_label),
            growth_dot.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(1, 0)),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Show "imaginary push" vector at the dot (perpendicular to real axis)
        push_arrow = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(1, 0),
            end=axes.c2p(1, 0.8),
            buff=0,
            color=BLUE,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        self.play(Create(push_arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Arc path showing the turn
        arc_path = Arc(radius=axes.get_x_unit_size(), start_angle=0, angle=PI/2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).move_to(axes.c2p(0,0), aligned_edge=ORIGIN)
        
        # Update dot and arrow for rotation
        rot_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_dot(d):
            angle = rot_tracker.get_value()
            d.move_to(axes.c2p(np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle)))
            
        def update_arrow(a):
            angle = rot_tracker.get_value()
            pos = axes.c2p(np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle))
            # Vector is tangent: (-sin, cos)
            dir_vec = np.array([-np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0])
            a.put_start_and_end_on(pos, pos + dir_vec * 0.8)

        growth_dot.add_updater(update_dot)
        push_arrow.add_updater(update_arrow)
        
        # Traced path for circular growth
        traced_path = TracedPath(growth_dot.get_center, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.add(traced_path)
        
        self.play(rot_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/4), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Label "Imaginary Push"
        push_text = Text("Imaginary Push", color="#00FFFF", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(push_text, "B5")
        push_arrow.set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        self.play(Write(push_text))
        self.play(rot_tracker.animate.set_value(3*PI/4), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PINK)
        
        # Angle indicator
        angle_arc = always_redraw(lambda: Arc(
            radius=0.4,
            start_angle=0,
            angle=rot_tracker.get_value(),
            color=PINK
        ).move_to(axes.c2p(0,0), aligned_edge=ORIGIN))
        
        # Use Text with unicode symbol for theta to avoid LaTeX dependency
        angle_label = Text("θ", color=PINK, font_size=24)
        
        # Position angle label near the arc
        def update_angle_label(l):
            angle = rot_tracker.get_value() / 2
            l.move_to(axes.c2p(0.6 * np.cos(angle), 0.6 * np.sin(angle)))
        
        angle_label.add_updater(update_angle_label)
        
        self.add(angle_arc, angle_label)
        self.play(rot_tracker.animate.set_value(2*PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        lines = [
            "Euler's formula links exponential growth to circular rotation.",
            "Angle theta determines our position on the unit circle.",
            "The real part is cosine of the angle.",
            "The imaginary part is sine of the angle.",
            "This formula bridges algebra and geometry perfectly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Master Formula: e^(iθ) = cos(θ) + i sin(θ)", lines)

        # Define Constants and Coordinate system
        theta_val = PI / 3
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1.2, 1.2, 1],
            y_range=[-1.2, 1.2, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_C}
        )
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "D4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Euler's formula links exponential growth to circular rotation.
        # Draw white unit circle and radius
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        unit_circle = Circle(radius=axes.x_axis.get_unit_size(), color=WHITE)
        unit_circle.move_to(axes.c2p(0,0))
        
        radius_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(0, 0),
            axes.c2p(np.cos(theta_val), np.sin(theta_val)),
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        self.play(Create(unit_circle), Create(radius_line), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Angle theta determines our position on the unit circle.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        angle_arc = Arc(
            radius=0.5,
            start_angle=0,
            angle=theta_val,
            arc_center=axes.c2p(0, 0),
            color=YELLOW
        )
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        theta_label = Text("θ", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)
        # Position label relative to arc
        theta_label.move_to(axes.c2p(0.4 * np.cos(theta_val/2), 0.4 * np.sin(theta_val/2)))
        
        self.play(Create(angle_arc), Write(theta_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The real part is cosine of the angle.
        # Highlight horizontal component in red
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED)
        )
        
        cos_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(0, 0),
            axes.c2p(np.cos(theta_val), 0),
            color=RED,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        cos_text = Text("cos(θ)", color=RED, font_size=24)
        cos_text.next_to(cos_line, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(cos_line), Write(cos_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The imaginary part is sine of the angle.
        # Highlight vertical component in blue
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(BLUE)
        )
        
        sin_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(np.cos(theta_val), 0),
            axes.c2p(np.cos(theta_val), np.sin(theta_val)),
            color=BLUE,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        sin_text = Text("i sin(θ)", color=BLUE, font_size=24)
        sin_text.next_to(sin_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(sin_line), Write(sin_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This formula bridges algebra and geometry perfectly.
        # Label the intersection and Fade in the formula at top
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Label intersection point
        point_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(np.cos(theta_val), np.sin(theta_val)), color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        point_label = Text("cos(θ) + i sin(θ)", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        point_label.next_to(point_dot, UR, buff=0.05)
        
        # Final Formula at Top Area
        master_formula = Text("e^(iθ) = cos(θ) + i sin(θ)", font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(master_formula, "A2", "A5")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(point_dot),
            Write(point_label),
            FadeIn(master_formula, shift=DOWN)
        )
        self.wait(2)

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("The Bridge Between Worlds: Euler's Formula", font_size=36)
        title.to_edge(UP)
        self.add(title)

        # Left-side Lecture Content
        lecture_points = VGroup(
            Text("• Connects Exponentials & Trig", font_size=24),
            Text("• The Complex Plane (Re, Im)", font_size=24),
            Text("• Rotation by Angle θ", font_size=24),
            Text("• Euler's Identity: e^(iπ) = -1", font_size=24),
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        lecture_points.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5).shift(DOWN * 0.5)

        # Right-side Animation Area (Axes)
        axes = ComplexPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        ).to_edge(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        
        # Use Text instead of strings to avoid LaTeX compilation dependency
        labels = axes.get_axis_labels(
            x_label=Text("Re", font_size=24), 
            y_label=Text("Im", font_size=24)
        )
        circle = Circle(radius=axes.x_axis.get_unit_size(), color=BLUE_B).move_to(axes.get_origin())
        
        # Math Expressions - Using Text with unicode characters to avoid LaTeX requirement
        formula = Text("e^iθ = cos(θ) + i sin(θ)", font_size=30)
        formula.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        identity = Text("e^iπ + 1 = 0", color=YELLOW, font_size=36)
        identity.next_to(lecture_points, DOWN, buff=1.0).align_to(lecture_points, LEFT)

        # Animations
        self.play(Write(lecture_points), Create(axes), Write(labels))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(Create(circle))
        
        # Moving Point
        dot = Dot(axes.n2p(1 + 0j), color=RED)
        line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(axes.get_origin(), dot.get_center(), color=WHITE))
        # Use Text instead of MathTex
        angle_label = always_redraw(
            lambda: Text("θ", font_size=24).move_to(
                axes.get_origin() + 0.6 * np.array([np.cos(line.get_angle()/2), np.sin(line.get_angle()/2), 0])
            )
        )
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Create(line), FadeIn(angle_label))
        
        # Animate theta from 0 to pi
        theta_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(axes.n2p(np.exp(1j * theta_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Highlight the final position (-1)
        self.play(Indicate(dot, scale_factor=2))
        self.play(Write(identity))
        
        self.wait(3)

        # Cleanup
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(title, lecture_points, axes, labels, circle, formula, dot, line, angle_label, identity)))

class Section6Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Create Euler's Identity components using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        # We use a VGroup to maintain the same indexing structure as the original code
        identity = VGroup(
            Text("e", font_size=120),      # 0
            Text("i", font_size=80),       # 1 (Part of superscript)
            Text("π", font_size=80),       # 2 (Part of superscript)
            Text("+", font_size=120),      # 3
            Text("1", font_size=120),      # 4
            Text("=", font_size=120),      # 5
            Text("0", font_size=120)       # 6
        )

        # Manually position components to simulate e^{iπ} + 1 = 0
        identity[1].next_to(identity[0].get_top(), RIGHT, buff=0.05).shift(DOWN * 0.2)
        identity[2].next_to(identity[1], RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        identity[3].next_to(identity[0], RIGHT, buff=1.3)
        identity[4].next_to(identity[3], RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        identity[5].next_to(identity[4], RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        identity[6].next_to(identity[5], RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        
        # Center the entire group on the screen
        identity.center()

        # Apply colors to the constants as specified in the original logic
        identity[0].set_color(YELLOW)  # e
        identity[1].set_color(PURPLE)  # i
        identity[2].set_color(BLUE)    # π
        identity[3].set_color(WHITE)   # +
        identity[4].set_color(GREEN)   # 1
        identity[5].set_color(WHITE)   # =
        identity[6].set_color(RED)     # 0

        # Animation sequence
        self.play(Write(identity))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Bridge Between Worlds: Euler's Formula and the Identity e^(πi) = -1
outline.target_audience: Advanced high school students or early university students

sections.title: The Mystery Meeting
sections.content: Introduce the three mathematical giants: 'e' (the king of growth), 'π' (the ruler of circles), and 'i' (the imaginary unit). Set the stage for how these three seemingly unrelated numbers collide in a single, elegant equation.
sections.example: Imagine a character named 'Pixel the Penguin' standing at a crossroads where three paths labeled 'Algebra', 'Geometry', and 'Calculus' meet. He finds a locked chest that can only be opened by combining these three unique keys.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Complex Playground
sections.content: Review the Complex Plane. Explain the Real axis (horizontal) and the Imaginary axis (vertical). Clarify that multiplying by 'i' represents a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation.
sections.example: Visualize a compass where North is 'i', South is '-i', East is '1', and West is '-1'. Pixel the Penguin turns 90 degrees every time he encounters an 'i' multiplier.

sections.title: Growth vs. Rotation: The Role of 'e'
sections.content: Contrast real-power growth (e^x) with imaginary-power growth (e^ix). Explain that while 'e' usually means growing outward, adding 'i' to the exponent changes 'pushing outward' into 'pushing sideways'—leading to rotation.
sections.example: Show a rocket ship. Normal 'e' is the engine pushing it straight up (growth). Adding 'i' is like a side-thruster that keeps the ship at a constant distance from the center, forcing it into a circular orbit.

sections.title: The Master Formula: e^(iθ) = cos(θ) + i sin(θ)
sections.content: Introduce Euler's Formula. Use a Unit Circle to show that any point on the circle can be described by an angle (θ). Show how 'cos' gives the real position and 'sin' gives the imaginary position.
sections.example: An animation of a lighthouse beam rotating. The tip of the beam traces a circle. At any angle θ, the beam's position is exactly e to the power of (i times θ).

sections.title: The Grand Finale: Walking π Distance
sections.content: Substitute θ with π (180 degrees). Show visually on the unit circle that traveling a distance of π radians (half a circle) lands you exactly at the point -1 on the real axis.
sections.example: Pixel the Penguin starts at '1' on the map. He follows the command e^(πi), which tells him to walk halfway around the circle. He stops, looks down, and sees he is standing exactly on the number '-1'.

sections.title: The Beauty of Unity
sections.content: Summarize the identity e^(πi) + 1 = 0. Highlight how it connects five fundamental constants: 0, 1, e, i, and π in one perfect harmony.
sections.example: A final graphic where the three paths from the beginning merge into a single golden bridge, showing the interconnectedness of all mathematics.

storyboard.title: The Mystery Meeting
lecture_lines: Three math giants meet at a strange crossroads.
Meet e for growth, pi for circles, i for imaginary.
Together, they unlock a beautiful secret of the universe.

Create 'e' (gold #FFD700), 'π' (silver #C0C0C0), and 'i' (cyan #00FFFF) with labels.
Scale the three symbols up and merge them into a central glow.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Complex Playground
lecture_lines: The complex plane has real and imaginary axes.
Multiplying by i rotates us 90 degrees counter-clockwise.
It is a playground where numbers can turn and spin.
animations: Draw white (#FFFFFF) axes with 'Real' and 'Imaginary' labels.
Move a white (#FFFFFF) dot from (1,0) to (0,1) along a 90-degree arc.
Add a spinning circular arrow around the origin in silver (#C0C0C0).

storyboard.title: Growth vs. Rotation: The Role of 'e'
lecture_lines: Real powers of e represent continuous outward growth.
But an imaginary power i changes the direction.
Instead of growing larger, the value starts to turn.
It is like a side-thruster creating a circular orbit.
Constant speed, but always changing the movement angle.
animations: Create a white (#FFFFFF) dot moving right along a line using a thruster [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/thruster.svg], leaving a fading trail.
Show a cyan (#00FFFF) 'i' appearing in the exponent, with a perpendicular arrow.
Transform the straight path into a counter-clockwise arc around the origin.
Draw a circular orbit path [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orbit.svg] in silver (#C0C0C0) that the dot follows.
Add a rotating radius line with a green (#00FF00) angle label θ.

storyboard.title: The Master Formula: e^(iθ) = cos(θ) + i sin(θ)
lecture_lines: Euler's formula links exponential growth to circular rotation.
Angle theta determines our position on the unit circle.
The real part is cosine of the angle.
The imaginary part is sine of the angle.
This formula bridges algebra and geometry perfectly.
animations: Draw a white (#FFFFFF) unit circle and a radius line.
Label the angle as θ in green (#00FF00) and move the radius.
Highlight the horizontal projection as cos(θ) in red (#FF0000).
Highlight the vertical projection as sin(θ) in blue (#0000FF).
Fade in the formula e^(iθ) = cos(θ) + i sin(θ) at the top.

storyboard.title: The Grand Finale: Walking π Distance
lecture_lines: Now, let us walk a distance of pi.
This represents a half-turn around the circle.
We start at one on the real axis.
Halfway around, we land exactly on negative one.
Therefore, e to the i pi equals negative one.
animations: Show a yellow (#FFFF00) arc of length π appearing above the circle.
Highlight the 180-degree semi-circle to show the turn.
Place a white (#FFFFFF) point at (1, 0) on the Real axis.
Animate the point moving to (-1, 0) along the arc.
Display the identity e^(πi) = -1 in the center in gold (#FFD700).

storyboard.title: The Beauty of Unity
lecture_lines: Adding one to both sides equals zero.
Five fundamental constants unite in one elegant equation.
This is the most beautiful identity in mathematics.
animations: Transform e^(πi) = -1 into the equation e^(πi) + 1 = 0.
Sequentially scale and flash 'e', 'π', 'i', '1', and '0' for emphasis.
Draw a glowing golden (#FFD700) border around the entire identity.
